source: Lake & Baroni (2018) Generalization without Systematicity (SCAN)
finding: Seq2seq RNNs generalise when test commands are close to training ones, but fail when a new primitive must be combined systematically.
numbers: Random split: best net 99.8% on test (5-run mean). 'Add jump' split: best simple RNN under 1.5%; overall-best config 0.08%; best config for jump 1.2%.
limits: Toy grammar; 2018 RNNs, not Transformers or LLMs.
agent_relevance: Background test for reuse of a primitive in a new combination. Do not assume a newly named step composes for free.

source: Lake & Baroni (2018) Generalization without Systematicity (SCAN), data coverage
finding: Generalisation to unseen commands rises sharply with the share of commands seen in training (random-split experiment).
numbers: 1% of commands: about 5% correct on new commands; 2%: about 54%; 4%: about 93%; 80%: 99.8%. Learning 'jump' from 8 vs 32 composed commands: 38.3% vs 88.4%.
limits: This is interpolation, not systematicity. Training fixed at 100k presentations.
agent_relevance: Few distinct composed examples matter more than repeats. Relevant to choosing prompt exemplars.

source: Lake & Baroni (2018) Generalization without Systematicity (SCAN), length split
finding: Networks cannot produce action sequences longer than seen in training.
numbers: Length split: best config 20.8% average (GRU with attention); overall-best 13.8%. Accuracy by sequence length ranged from 95.76% for 24-action commands to 22.8% for the longest.
limits: Same limits as above.
agent_relevance: Productivity (longer than seen) is a separate weakness. Keep step counts and nesting depth under program control.

source: Kim & Linzen (2020) COGS: A Compositional Generalization Challenge
finding: Transformers and LSTMs score near perfect in distribution but poorly on structural and lexical generalisation, with high seed variance.
numbers: In-distribution accuracy 96-99%. Generalisation accuracy 16-35%. Seed variance about 6-8% standard deviation.
quote: in-distribution accuracy on the COGS test set was near-perfect (96-99%)
limits: Small semantic-parsing fragment; models trained from scratch, no large pretraining.
agent_relevance: A pass on the training distribution says nothing about reuse in new syntactic roles. Test on held-out roles, not just held-out items.

source: Keysers et al. (2020) CFQ: Measuring compositional generalization
finding: Accuracy falls as compound novelty rises while atoms stay familiar; compound divergence is a better predictor than length ratio.
numbers: R2 between compound divergence and accuracy 0.81-0.88; R2 for input or output length ratio 0.11-0.22. Three architectures (LSTM+attention, Transformer, Universal Transformer), 5 runs each. MCD splits keep atom divergence near 0.02.
limits: Exact MCD accuracy table was garbled in my text extraction, so not recorded here. No LLM prompts.
agent_relevance: A recipe for our own systematicity tests: control compound novelty, not length.

source: Keysers et al. (2020) CFQ, tuning protocol
finding: Authors tune hyperparameters on a random split only, because tuning on the test-type split would leak the test distribution.
numbers: Each experiment replicated 5 times, mean accuracy with 95% confidence intervals.
limits: Methodological point, no new effect.
agent_relevance: Do not tune the scaffold on the very items used to score it.

source: Hupkes et al. (2020) Compositionality decomposed (PCFG SET)
finding: Five tests (systematicity, productivity, substitutivity, localism, overgeneralisation) show models fail in different ways.
numbers: Systematicity score drops from overall accuracy by 33% (LSTM), 34% (ConvS2S), 22% (Transformer). Test samples 11 thousand, 3 runs.
limits: Synthetic grammar; seq2seq from scratch; authors warn against general claims about architectures.
agent_relevance: Useful taxonomy for testing our agent: novel pairs, longer chains, nested structure.

source: Hupkes et al. (2020) productivity test
finding: Removing long sequences from training collapses accuracy; Transformer is the most productive but still poor.
numbers: Drop of 62% (LSTM), 64% (ConvS2S), 46% (Transformer); Transformer falls to mean accuracy 0.50, LSTM 0.30, ConvS2S 0.31.
limits: Synthetic data.
agent_relevance: Do not expect the model to extend a procedure to more steps than shown in exemplars.

source: Hupkes et al. (2020) rules versus exceptions
finding: Whether a model learns an exception depends on how often it appears; at very low rates it is not memorised, at 0.5% there is almost no overgeneralisation.
numbers: Exception rates 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5%. At 0.1% the Transformer applies the rule to 88% of exceptions at some point in training (LSTM 68%, ConvS2S 79%).
limits: Synthetic; rate chosen by design.
agent_relevance: Rare exceptions need explicit mention in the scaffold, since the model's default is the rule.

source: Lake & Baroni (2023) Human-like systematic generalization through a meta-learning neural network, Nature
finding: A standard Transformer trained on a stream of compositional tasks (MLC) matches human systematicity in a few-shot instruction task. Direct reply to Fodor and Pylyshyn.
numbers: Humans n=25: 80.7% exact algebraic outputs on systematic queries and 72.5% on longer outputs. MLC sampling: 82.4% and 77.8%. Errors that are one-to-one translations: MLC 56.3%, people 24.4%.
quote: only MLC achieves both the systematicity and flexibility needed for human-like generalization
limits: Models adult skill, not its acquisition; cannot emit new symbols; untested on full natural language.
agent_relevance: Systematicity comes from training on varying word meanings, not from scale. A prompt-only agent needs explicit decomposition.

source: Lake & Baroni (2023) MLC, benchmarks
finding: MLC nearly solves lexical splits of SCAN and COGS, but fails on structural ones.
numbers: SCAN: three systematic splits at error 0.22% or lower. COGS: error 0.87% over 18 lexical types. Plain seq2seq with the same Transformer: error at least 7 times higher. SCAN length split and three COGS structural types: 100% error.
quote: MLC fails to handle longer output sequences (SCAN length split) as well as novel and more complex sentence structures
limits: Success is lexical. Preliminary GPT-4 tests in the supplement left systematicity as open.
agent_relevance: Even trained systematicity does not give productivity. Keep nesting and length handled by code.

source: Zhou et al. (2023) Least-to-most prompting enables complex reasoning in LLMs
finding: Decompose a command into sub-commands, then solve in order with earlier answers in context. Closes the SCAN length-split gap with 14 exemplars.
numbers: code-davinci-002 on SCAN length split: standard 16.7%, chain of thought 16.2%, least-to-most 99.7%. text-davinci-002: 6.0, 0.0, 76.0 (100-command subset). code-davinci-001: 0.4, 0.0, 60.7.
quote: at least 99% using just 14 exemplars, compared to only 16% accuracy with chain-of-thought prompting
limits: One toy benchmark; hand-written decomposition prompt per task; strongest with a code-pretrained model.
agent_relevance: Direct support for a program-run decompose-then-solve operator rather than free chain of thought.

source: Zhou et al. (2023) least-to-most, SCAN errors
finding: Remaining SCAN errors are scope errors on nested modifiers.
numbers: 13 failures in the length test set: 6 mis-scoped 'twice' or 'thrice' after 'around' (for example x9 instead of x12), the rest read 'after' as 'and'.
limits: One model, code-davinci-002.
agent_relevance: Nested repetition is where LLMs slip. Let code do the multiplication of nested counts.

source: Press et al. (2023) Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap
finding: Models often answer both sub-questions of a 2-hop question yet fail the composed one. The gap stays about 40% across GPT-3 sizes.
numbers: Compositional Celebrities: 8.6k 2-hop questions. Gap roughly constant near 40% for GPT-3 sizes. Measured gap: ChatGPT 42.9%, GPT-4 23.0%.
limits: Questions use improbable fact pairs. Needs the model to know each single hop.
agent_relevance: A measurable quantity: gap = share of cases where both hops are right but the composition is wrong. Track it for our agent.

source: Press et al. (2023) self-ask
finding: Asking the model to write follow-up sub-questions and answer them before the final answer narrows the gap; plugging in a search engine helps more.
numbers: Exact accuracies for Bamboogle, 2WikiMultiHop and Musique were not cleanly extractable from the PDF table, so none recorded; the paper reports self-ask plus search is the best of its Davinci-002 variants.
limits: Hand-tuned prompt on training set; table cells hard to align in PDF text.
agent_relevance: Explicit sub-question steps with external lookup per hop is a usable operator.

source: Dziri et al. (2023) Faith and Fate: Limits of Transformers on Compositionality
finding: LLMs solve compositional tasks by matching linearised subgraphs, not by systematic procedures; accuracy falls toward zero as computation depth grows.
numbers: Tasks: multi-digit multiplication, logic grid puzzles, dynamic programming. Models: GPT-3, ChatGPT, GPT-4, LLaMA, FlanT5 in zero-shot, few-shot and finetuned settings.
quote: transformer LLMs solve compositional tasks by reducing multi-step compositional reasoning into linearized subgraph matching
limits: Three task families; 2023 models.
agent_relevance: Deep chains fail even for the best models. Cap chain depth and verify each step.

source: Dziri et al. (2023) Faith and Fate, hidden errors
finding: Correct final answers often hide wrong intermediate steps, which points to memorisation of frequent input-output patterns.
numbers: 82.3% of correct final answers on 4-digit by 2-digit multiplication (not in training) had at least one error in the computation graph.
limits: Multiplication only for this figure.
agent_relevance: A right answer is not proof of a sound process. Check steps with code, not just the final answer.

source: Gao et al. (2023) PAL: Program-aided Language Models
finding: The model writes a program as its reasoning and an interpreter executes it: a symbolic thought medium inside an LLM loop.
numbers: GSM8K: PAL beats PaLM-540B chain of thought by about 15 points absolute (as stated by authors). Object counting 96.7%, +23.7 over CoT.
limits: Works where the task is expressible as code; benchmark leakage not fully excluded; exact table cells garbled.
agent_relevance: Offload exact symbol work to code. Matches our rule that the program decides and the model fills slots.

source: Gao et al. (2023) PAL, GSM-HARD
finding: With larger numbers, chain of thought collapses but programs hold up, so the failure was arithmetic, not logic.
numbers: GSM-HARD: direct 19.7% to 5.0%; chain of thought 65.6% to 20.1% (relative drop almost 70%); PAL stays 61.5% (drops 14.3%). In 16 of 25 analysed cases CoT wrote nearly identical reasoning for easy and hard numbers.
limits: 25 cases analysed by hand.
agent_relevance: Plan in language, compute in code.

source: Wong et al. (2023) From Word Models to World Models (probabilistic Language of Thought)
finding: An LLM translates language into probabilistic-program code and a symbolic engine does the inference; an explicit probabilistic language of thought built on an LLM.
numbers: Four domains: probabilistic reasoning, logical and relational reasoning, visual and physical reasoning, social reasoning about agents. Mostly worked examples, few benchmark scores.
limits: Hand-built generative model per domain; examples are illustrative.
agent_relevance: Pattern for states needing uncertainty: write the model as code, then query it. Costly to build per task.

source: Ellis (2023) Human-like Few-Shot Learning via Bayesian Reasoning over Natural Language
finding: An LLM proposes hypotheses in natural language and a prior and likelihood reweigh them, making natural language the hypothesis language.
numbers: 100 proposals per batch explain 81% of variance in human judgments (R2 = .81), better than GPT-4 alone, within 3% of human accuracy on the task; beats a Bayesian program-learning baseline with about 10^9 sampling moves.
quote: our model explains 81% of the variance in human responses
limits: Prior tuned on human data and was critical; tasks are number and set concepts.
agent_relevance: Propose-many then score with an outside selector, which fits our candidate plus check design.

source: Ellis et al. (2021) DreamCoder: wake-sleep Bayesian program learning
finding: A system that grows its own library of named symbolic abstractions and a neural search guide; the nearest AI build of a learned language of thought.
numbers: Text editing (SyGuS): 3.7% solved in 10 min before learning, 79.6% after; CVC4 82.4%; DreamCoder with large budget 84.3%. Graphics and towers: no other model above 60% of held-out tasks, DreamCoder nearly 100%. After 8 wake-sleep cycles it learns 93% of the physics laws and identities.
limits: Hand-given primitives; small domains.
agent_relevance: Reusable verified sub-routines speed later search. Analogue: store checked operators and reuse them.

source: Mahowald et al. (2024) Dissociating language and thought in LLMs
finding: LLMs are strong at formal linguistic competence but unreliable at functional competence (reasoning, world knowledge, social); human brains dissociate the two.
numbers: Review, no single effect size.
limits: Review of models up to 2023.
agent_relevance: Fluent text is not evidence of structured thought; keep control and checks outside the model.

source: Webb, Holyoak & Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: GPT-3 matches or beats humans on text digit-matrix analogies and is weaker on story analogies.
numbers: Zero-generalisation matrix problems: GPT-3 vs humans OR=1.76, p=0.0007, CI [1.27, 2.46]. Story analogies, near condition: humans better, OR=0.37, p=0.0003; 15 of 54 humans chose the analogous story on every trial.
limits: text-davinci-003; GPT-4 only preliminary; later work challenged contamination.
agent_relevance: Some rule induction exists without scaffolds; verify with altered problems.

source: Berglund et al. (2024) The Reversal Curse
finding: Models trained on 'A is B' do not infer 'B is A', unlike a structured, systematic representation.
numbers: GPT-4: 79% for 'Who is the celebrity's parent', 33% for the reverse (1000 celebrities). Fine-tuned Llama-1: above 80% in the trained direction, below 7% reversed (near chance). Not fixed by size or augmentation.
quote: if "A is B" appears in-context, models can deduce the reverse relationship
limits: If the fact is in the prompt, reversal works.
agent_relevance: Put needed facts in context in the direction needed.

source: Hao et al. (2024) Coconut: reasoning in a continuous latent space
finding: Feeding hidden states back instead of words beats chain of thought on a search-heavy logic task, arguing a words-only thought medium can bottleneck planning.
numbers: GSM8k: Coconut 34.1% vs no-CoT 16.5% (CoT is higher, 42.9%). ProsQA (graph search): Coconut 97.0% vs CoT 77.5%. Continuous thoughts appear to hold several next steps, like breadth-first search.
limits: Needs curriculum training; GPT-2 scale; table read from garbled extraction.
agent_relevance: Shows a limit of verbal scaffolds on search. We cannot train, so keep search in code.
